title: The H1 must be followed by a summary blockquote
rationale: conformance_testable is false, per the divergence recorded in policy_note: the spec's own prose marks only the H1 as strictly required. Verified against a live fetch of https://llmstxt.org/ on 2026-07-30. Corrects a prior defect: 'as would be immediately useful to an LLM' was fabricated and does not appear on the page; the real item 3 also reads 'the project', not 'the project or site'. RE-PINNED 2026-10-07 to v2 (AnswerDotAI/llms-txt @6e55a65, nbs/index.qmd) after a full re-read: the Format list is byte-identical to v1 (v1 lines 40-46 equal v2 lines 49-55), so the quote is unchanged and now sits at source line 52. v2 rewrote only the surrounding prose (path scope, the "Optional" section, .md naming, link relations, the RFC 8615 rationale), none of which this rule reads.

derivedFrom.version: llmstxt.org, the llms.txt proposal v2 (date-modified 2026-08-10) as published at AnswerDotAI/llms-txt commit 6e55a65a (first transcribed 2026-07-16 from v1 at c7178b9d, re-verified against the pinned blob 2026-07-30, re-pinned to v2 after a re-read 2026-10-07)
derivedFrom.quote: A blockquote with a short summary of the project, containing key information necessary for understanding the rest of the file

policy_note: Migrated verbatim from the pre-pilot validate-llms-txt.mjs:69-72, a file atlas decision 0119 D2 has since retired into audits/checks/b2-llms.mjs (the quotation below is a historical record and is reproduced unchanged): 'required by this validator; the spec's own prose marks only the H1 as strictly required, but every real-world llms.txt -- including this site's -- includes it, and the team's validator contract treats it as required.' This is a declared, reviewable local convention, not a claim about llmstxt.org conformance.
applicability: An llms.txt body whose first non-blank line is a valid H1.
expectation: The next non-blank line after the H1 matches /^>\s+\S/.

cases.name: H1 present, nothing at all follows (bqLine is null, not merely non-matching)

known-answer fixture: an unlinked URL, a dangling section, and no blockquote all flag together (REVERSAL 2 -- a shared multi-violation input is a legal failed case; its expect lists every id the input emits). The fixture moved to v2 violations in the same commit as the v2 relaxation: under v1 it used a bare bullet with no URL and a prose-only section, both legal now, which would have quietly reduced this case to a single-violation input.
